business_problem: System1 needed to modernize MapQuest's points-of-interest search stack so it could scale beyond costly in-memory storage and support more intelligent recommendations.
solution_summary: After acquiring MapQuest, System1 replatformed the service's points-of-interest data onto MongoDB Atlas to create a simpler, more scalable search architecture. The team started with a lift-and-shift of JSON documents, then consolidated source data, metadata, logs, and more than 95 million information sheets in Atlas so information that is frequently accessed together could live together. Atlas now runs on Amazon Web Services and provides the base for MapQuest's expanded search stack. System1 is experimenting with Atlas Vector Search to support semantic queries such as intent-based requests for nearby businesses, while geospatial operators and aggregation pipelines combine location context with POI relevance. Because Atlas also provides point-in-time recovery and security controls, System1 can evolve the experience incrementally without interrupting users. The result is a faster, more flexible platform that turns legacy POI data into discoverable, recommendation-ready search experiences.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores MapQuest's POI documents, metadata, logs, and developer-site data in one scalable managed platform.

solution_components.name: Atlas Vector Search
solution_components.role: Enables semantic and intent-based retrieval for richer POI discovery and recommendations.

data_flow: POI source data, metadata, logs, and developer-site content are consolidated into MongoDB Atlas, where Atlas Vector Search and geospatial operators retrieve and rank nearby businesses or intent-based matches before those results are returned to MapQuest users.
business_outcome: System1 improved POI query performance, created a foundation for semantic search and recommendation features, and gave MapQuest a more cost-effective platform for 30 million monthly users.
